neighbours.label: a first- or second-person, present-tense statement of the speaker's or addressee's own situation, as in the set-up of a question or request ('I'm planning…', 'You're hosting…', 'My landlord is asking me…'); third-person past narrative stays quiet
fire: I'm moving to a new flat in March and need to hire a van.
You're driving home late at night and a tyre goes flat.
My neighbour is asking me to cut down a tree on my side of the fence.
I'm thinking of buying a used bike for my commute to work.
You're offered two jobs in the same week and must choose by Friday.
We're trying to book a hall for my parents' anniversary in May.
I'm cooking for twelve people on Sunday and my oven is tiny.
My boss is asking me to work weekends for the next two months.
quiet: He moved to a new flat in March and hired a van.
The driver went home late that night after the tyre was fixed.
The neighbour cut down a tree on his side of the fence.
She bought a used bike for her commute to work.
The clerk was offered two jobs that week and chose by Friday.
They booked a hall for the anniversary in May.
The cook fed twelve people on Sunday with a tiny oven.
The manager worked weekends for the next two months.

notes: Top examples are the opening words of interview questions and 'Q:' set-ups; in probes the Q:/interviewer tag was not needed ('I'm planning a trip…' fired 0.50 without it, 0.57 with it), while the third-person past version scored 0.04. Broad pole (1% of tokens reach 0.1 of max), so middling scores are expected.
